about.title: Redlands Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A faulty product doesn't announce itself. It might be a space heater in an older home off Orange Street, a power tool bought for a weekend project, a car component that fails on I-10 near the Alabama Street exit, or a children's item that never should have reached a shelf. When something you trusted causes harm in Redlands, California law gives you a notable advantage: product liability claims usually run on strict liability. You generally don't have to prove the manufacturer was careless, only that the product had a design, manufacturing, or warning defect and that the defect caused your injury. Redlands is home to about 71,000 people in San Bernardino County. Public records list 477 injury collisions here in 2025, and some crashes involve airbags, tires, or brakes that didn't perform as designed. Keep the product, the packaging, and any receipts. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm; we connect you with an independent attorney who takes product cases on contingency, so there's no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Redlands Residents Turn to LawProactive for Product Cases

items.title: Strict liability works in your favor
items.desc: In California, a defective-product claim generally turns on whether the product had a design, manufacturing, or warning defect that caused your injury, not on proving the maker was negligent. An attorney in our network knows how to frame the case around the defect itself.

items.title: More than one company may be responsible
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all share liability under California law. The attorney you're connected with can identify every link in the chain that put the product in your hands.

items.title: Preserving the evidence is step one
items.desc: The damaged product, its packaging, and any instructions or warnings are often the heart of the claim. We connect you quickly so an independent attorney can help you protect that evidence before it's lost or repaired.

items.question: A part on my car failed while I was driving on I-10 through Redlands. Is that a crash case or a product case?
items.answer: It can be both. If a component such as a brake, tire, or airbag didn't perform the way it was designed to, a product liability claim against the manufacturer or seller may exist alongside any claim involving another driver. Don't have the vehicle repaired or scrapped until an attorney has had a chance to look at it, because the failed part is key evidence.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer did something wrong?
items.answer: Usually not. California product liability often runs on strict liability, which means you generally need to show the product was defective in its design, manufacturing, or warnings and that the defect caused your injury. Whether the company was careful or careless is typically not the deciding question.

items.question: I still have the product that hurt me. What should I do with it?
items.answer: Keep it exactly as it is, along with the box, manual, receipt, and any photos of the injury or scene. Don't try to fix it, return it, or let the store take it back. An independent attorney connected through LawProactive can arrange for it to be examined properly; our service is free and the attorney works on contingency.
